subject: mathematics_2a
question_text: If z = 3 − 5i, then show that z³ − 10z² + 58z − 136 = 0.

mark_split.label: Form the quadratic z² − 6z + 34 = 0 from z = 3 − 5i

recall_prompt: Say how you would show the cubic is zero — what quadratic you build from z first, how you use it inside the cubic, and why the whole thing collapses to zero.
insider_note: Do not substitute 3 − 5i into the cubic — build the real quadratic z² − 6z + 34 = 0 first and factor the cubic as (z − 4)(z² − 6z + 34). Half the marks are that factorisation, and the last mark is the sentence that says the second bracket is zero.

steps.label: Build the quadratic
steps.margin_note: First mark. Do not substitute 3 − 5i into the cubic — that is a long, error-prone expansion. Instead move the 3 across, square to remove i, and get a real quadratic that z satisfies.
steps.memory_tip: Move the 3 across and square: (−5i)² = −25 gives the real quadratic z² − 6z + 34 = 0.

recall.must_convey: That z − 3 = −5i is squared to give z² − 6z + 9 = −25, so z satisfies z² − 6z + 34 = 0.
accept: move the three across, square both sides and get z squared minus six z plus thirty four equals zero
z minus three is minus five i, squaring gives z squared minus six z plus nine equals minus twenty five
build the quadratic z squared minus six z plus thirty four from z equals three minus five i
z minus three square cheste minus twenty five, so z square minus six z plus thirty four equals zero
square z minus three to remove the i and get a real quadratic

steps.why: Squaring −5i gives −25, a real number, so the i disappears and z is seen to satisfy a real quadratic. The cubic in the question is built from that quadratic, which is why this line does most of the work.
common_mistakes: Squaring z = 3 − 5i directly instead of z − 3 = −5i, which keeps an i term.
Ending at z² − 6z + 9 = −25 without moving the 25 across.

steps.label: Factor the cubic
steps.margin_note: Half the marks. The cubic is (z − 4) times the quadratic from (1). Either divide the cubic by z² − 6z + 34 (quotient z − 4) or, faster to write, multiply out (z − 4)(z² − 6z + 34) and show it matches term by term.
steps.memory_tip: The cubic is (z − 4) times that quadratic. Check: −6z² − 4z² = −10z² and 34z + 24z = 58z.

recall.must_convey: That the cubic z³ − 10z² + 58z − 136 equals (z − 4)(z² − 6z + 34), shown by division or by multiplying out.
accept: the cubic factors as z minus four times z squared minus six z plus thirty four
divide the cubic by the quadratic and the quotient is z minus four with no remainder
multiply z minus four by the quadratic and you get back the cubic exactly
cubic ni z minus four into quadratic ga rayochu
write the cubic as z minus four times z squared minus six z plus thirty four
heard_as: z squared minus six z plus thirty four

steps.why: The question is designed so that the quadratic from step 1 is a factor of the cubic. Showing the factorisation is the whole proof — once the quadratic factor is zero, the product is zero regardless of the other factor.
common_mistakes: Getting the middle coefficient wrong: −6z² − 4z² = −10z² and 34z + 24z = 58z.
Guessing the factor (z − 4) and never checking that the product really equals the cubic.
Dividing and leaving a non-zero remainder because of an arithmetic slip, then carrying on anyway.

steps.label: Conclude
steps.margin_note: Last mark. Put (1) into the factored form: the second bracket is 0, so the product is 0.
steps.memory_tip: The second bracket is 0 by (1), so the product is 0. Write 'from (1)' beside the line.

recall.must_convey: That since z² − 6z + 34 = 0 from (1), the factored cubic is (z − 4) times zero, which is zero.
accept: the quadratic bracket is zero from equation one so the whole product is zero
z minus four times zero is zero, hence the cubic is zero
substitute the quadratic equals zero and the cubic reduces to zero
second bracket zero kabatti product zero, hence proved
one factor is zero so the cubic is zero

steps.why: A product with a zero factor is zero. That is the entire logic, and writing 'from (1)' beside it shows the examiner exactly where the zero came from.
common_mistakes: Trying to also show z − 4 = 0, which is false and not needed.
